title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. X is a smooth proper connected complex curve of genus g>=2, and Pi = pi_1(X). The canonical flat torsor P comes from uniformization: Pi embeds in G' = GP(1,R), the real projective group acting on the Poincaré half-plane. G = SL(2,R). There is a central extension 1 -> Z = Z/2 -> G -> G' -> 1. The subscript d means the same group with the discrete topology; G_d -> G, Z_d -> Z and G'_d -> G' are the identity maps.

Problem served. The previous page asks for a canonical algebraic integrable connection on P(Omega^{-1}+Omega), the projectivisation of a rank-2 bundle that is an extension of Omega^{-1} by Omega. To realise the flat PGL2 torsor as the projectivisation of an actual rank-2 flat bundle, Pi -> G' must lift to SL(2,R). The page computes the obstruction to that lift.

Computation.
- The obstruction is the image of the generator xi of H^2(B_{G'},Z/2) = Z/2 under X -> B_Pi -> B_{G'_d} -> B_{G'}. It lands in H^2(Pi,Z/2) = H^2(X,Z/2) = Z/2.
- Both B_G and B_{G'} are homotopic to BS^1, with maximal compacts T = S^1 in SL and T' = S^1 = T/{±1} in G'. So H^2(B_G,Z) = Z with generator W (or E, the Euler class of T) and H^2(B_{G'},Z) = Z.
- The covering T -> T' is the squaring map, so the two generators differ by a factor 2. He writes this as 'E' = 1/2 E' and '·2'.
- The mod-2 reduction of the G' Euler class is xi, via a commutative square relating H^*(X,Z) <- H^*(B_{G'},Z) to H^2(X,Z/2) <- H^2(B_{G'},Z/2).
- Pulling the G' Euler class E' back to H^2(X,Z) = Z gives the Euler number of the uniformizing representation, ±(2g-2) (Milnor–Wood maximal value, the degree of the tangent bundle). In terms of the SL generator this is g-1, which he notes as '2g-2 ~> g-1'.
- Since 2g-2 is even, the mod-2 obstruction vanishes and the Fuchsian representation lifts to SL(2,R). The lifts form a torsor under H^1(X,Z/2), i.e. they correspond to theta characteristics Omega^{1/2}. The flat rank-2 bundle is then the extension of Omega^{-1/2} by Omega^{1/2}, whose projectivisation is P(Omega^{-1}+Omega).
- There are stray attempts with H^4(B_G,Z) and H^4(X,...); the latter is zero for a curve. They were abandoned or crossed out.

The page is a topological sanity check of the canonical uniformization (indigenous) bundle and its liftability, within notes whose next page returns to divided-power algebra.
errors: If G' were PGL(2,R) (disconnected, maximal compact O(2)), H^2(B_{G'},Z) would be Z/2, not Z. The statement H^2(B_{G'},Z) = Z requires G' = PSL(2,R), the identity component, which is where Pi actually lands.

The factor-2 bookkeeping is ambiguous. Under the squaring map T -> T' the generator of H^2(BT') pulls back to twice the generator of H^2(BT); writing E' = 1/2 E only makes sense after identifying both groups inside a common Q-vector space. The arrows labelled '2' are consistent with this reading but the notation is loose.
The lines with H^4(B_G,Z) and H^4(X,Z) = Z are erroneous or abandoned, since H^4 of a curve vanishes. They play no role in the final computation.
The sign of the Euler number (2g-2 versus 2-2g) depends on orientation conventions and is not tracked.

ideas.what: Obstruction to lifting the Fuchsian uniformizing representation Pi -> PSL(2,R) to SL(2,R) is the mod-2 Euler class; it vanishes because e = 2g-2 is even. Lifts correspond to theta characteristics (square roots of Omega).
ideas.modern_name: Lifting of Fuchsian groups to SL(2,R) / spin structures and theta characteristics
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré, Fricke–Klein); Milnor (1958), Wood (1971), Gunning (1967), Atiyah (spin structures, 1971)

ideas.what: Euler class of the flat PSL(2,R) bundle of uniformization equals 2g-2, computed via continuous versus discrete group classifying spaces (B_{G_d} -> B_G).
ideas.modern_name: Milnor–Wood maximal Euler class; Goldman's characterization of Fuchsian representations

ideas.what: Canonical flat PGL2 torsor on a curve, realised as the projectivisation of the extension of Omega^{-1/2} by Omega^{1/2} (context of the previous page).

missed.claim: Within notes on the divided-power de Rham complex (crystalline context, 1975-76), Grothendieck studies the canonical uniformizing flat PGL2 torsor and asks for an algebraic canonical integrable connection on P(Omega^{-1}+Omega). This is the indigenous-bundle / oper object that Mochizuki later made central to p-adic Teichmüller theory, and here it is juxtaposed with divided powers. The present page only does the classical topological check (liftability via theta characteristics), so nothing new is proved here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mild historical evidence that Grothendieck considered uniformization (indigenous) bundles alongside crystalline / divided-power methods well before Mochizuki. It is of interest to historians, not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is a standard (and correct) characteristic-class check that the Fuchsian representation lifts to SL(2,R). The only interest is historical: Grothendieck's attention to indigenous bundles inside crystalline notes.
transcription_corrections: G' is written 'G' = GP(1,R)' (projective group; must be PSL(2,R) for H^2(B_{G'},Z) = Z), not 'Gl(2,R)'.
In the bottom-left diagram the first group is 'Z ≃ H^2(X,Z)' — the image's '4' is likely a 2 or an abandoned H^4; similarly 'H^4(B_{G'},Z) ∋ W'' should probably read H^2.
'H^4(B_G,Z)' near the top is probably H^2(B_G,Z), partly overwritten, with the remark 'Z/2Z·2=0'.
'GP = G'' in the blue diagram: Pi ⊂ GP = G' ⊃ S^1 = T', and SL = G ⊃ S^1 = T.
